## Slide 2 — The Opportunity (Today vs. After)
opportunity_headline: Mobile Field Capture & Project Dashboards.
opportunity_summary: A connected tablet app that replaces paper field tickets, feeding live project, equipment, and fuel margin — so cost overruns get caught while the job is still open.
today_metric_1: −41.2 – +58.4% · Month-over-month EBITDA % swings, with little real-time visibility
today_metric_2: ~26 days · Reporting lag after project close prevents real-time intervention
today_pain_bullets:
- Foremen handwrite daily field tickets on paper; keyed into Excel next morning (12–24h lag)
- Fuel and equipment-hour entry is optional; ~52 active jobs live in disconnected workbooks
after_horizon: AFTER — TARGET IN ~16 WEEKS
after_metric_1: +1.6–2.7pp · EBITDA margin uplift — $1.5M–$2.6M / yr direct
after_metric_2: <24 hrs · Data latency — real-time field sync from job sites
after_capability_bullets:
- Connected tablet app with enforced daily fuel + equipment-hour capture and automatic job allocation
- Live per-job production and financial performance
build_summary: THE 16-WEEK BUILD
PHASE 1 · WKS 1–8 · FOUNDATION & PILOT — Cloud data warehouse + accounting connector, the Operations dashboard, and a single-crew field-capture pilot run in parallel with paper.
PHASE 2 · WKS 8–16 · FLEET ROLLOUT — Fleet-wide capture, the fuel/equipment-allocation engine, CEO / Finance dashboards with variance alerts, combined-entity reporting, and asset-tracking integration.

## Slide 3 — The Platform / Solution (numbered components)
platform_headline: One Operational Intelligence Platform, two connected layers.
platform_summary: A mobile capture layer that replaces clipboards, and an analytics layer that turns captured data into live metrics — layered on top of the accounting and asset systems, not replacing them.
components:
1.
  number: 01
  kicker: INPUTS · MOBILE FIELD CAPTURE
  title: Capture crew activity one time, in real-time.
  description: Connected tablet app: a guided, button-driven workflow with dependent dropdowns, the full earthwork + equipment-delay taxonomy, crew, and enforced fuel — buffering locally through connectivity dropouts.
2.
  number: 02
  kicker: DATA FOUNDATION
  title: Integrate into one data store.
  description: A cloud warehouse joining field data, fuel, and accounting financials. Accounting + GL/fuel-card connectors, asset-tracking and pipeline ingestion, scheduled batch where APIs are constrained.
3.
  number: 03
  kicker: OUTPUTS · DASHBOARDS & ALERTS
  title: Live project performance, role by role.
  description: Operations, CEO, and Finance dashboards with drill-down from fleet → job → crew → day.

## Slide 5 — Commercial Terms / How QofAI Gets Paid
terms_headline: A partnership built on performance.
terms_summary: We invest. We deliver. You retain the value. QofAI bears all up-front build, licensing, and hosting cost; the client only pays from realized EBITDA gains — and keeps the rest.
downside_protection: If margins don't improve above your locked baseline, QofAI earns nothing.
qofai_investment: $275,000 · Engineering, deployment, and all implementation risk — fully absorbed before the client pays a dollar. (unconfirmed, see gaps)
client_upfront: $0 · No capital outlay. No per-seat BI licensing. Tablets (~18, rugged cases) procured by client — not in contract.
comp_schedule: YEAR 1 20% · YEAR 2 10% · YEAR 3 5% · YEAR 4+ 0% · Capped at 2.5× initial investment or 3 years, whichever first; ~$19K/yr support after that.
client_retention: Client retains 80–84%, 100% thereafter.
value_mapping:
1.
  scenario: CONSERVATIVE
  ebitda_gain: +1.6pp · $1,500,000/yr
  qofai_comp: $640,000
  client_retained_ebitda: $3,600,000
  enterprise_value: $10,700,000
2.
  scenario: BASE CASE
  ebitda_gain: +2.2pp · $2,050,000/yr
  qofai_comp: $685,000
  client_retained_ebitda: $4,900,000
  enterprise_value: $14,000,000
3.
  scenario: OPTIMISTIC
  ebitda_gain: +2.7pp · $2,600,000/yr
  qofai_comp: $685,000 (cap)
  client_retained_ebitda: $6,200,000
  enterprise_value: $17,300,000
payment_mechanics [render under heading "HOW PAYMENT WORKS"]: Measured monthly. Actual job & fleet EBITDA margin is compared to the client's locked pre-launch baseline; improvement is expressed in margin points.
Converted to EBITDA. The margin-point gain is applied to financial performance at the contribution basis locked at signing for the term.
Share paid that month. QofAI receives the year's share (20% / 10% / 5%) of that figure — paid monthly until the 2.5× cap or the 3-year term.
terms_footnote: Enterprise value at exit assumes a 6× EBITDA multiple on the annual uplift, plus a 0.25× reporting-readiness multiple improvement on ~$6.9M adjusted EBITDA. Directional, for decision support.

## Slide 6 — Next Steps (numbered actions with owners)
next_steps_headline: Four moves to launch the build.
next_steps_summary: Each action has a named owner and a target week.
action_items:
1.
  number: 01
  week: WK 0
  owner: CLIENT LEADERSHIP
  title: Approve Project Plan
  description: Leadership reviews and approves the platform scope, the two-phase plan, and the 16-week timeline before the build begins.
2.
  number: 02
  week: WK 0
  owner: QOFAI + CLIENT LEADERSHIP
  title: Sign Performance-Based Contract
  description: Execute the performance-based agreement: QofAI bears all upfront cost and is paid from realized EBITDA gains, capped at 2.5× cost over a three-year term.
3.
  number: 03
  week: WK 1–2
  owner: QOFAI ENGINEERING
  title: Kick Off QofAI FDEs
  description: QofAI's forward-deployed engineers begin the build — standing up the cloud warehouse, the accounting connector, and the Operations dashboard.
4.
  number: 04
  week: WK 1–2
  owner: OPERATIONS
  title: Select the pilot crew & foreman
  description: Choose a tech-receptive foreman for the single-crew pilot; lock Phase 1 scope to the daily ticket, fuel, and the financial dashboard.
